solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Loyalist beginning to accept law-breaking

indicators.note: to accept something is to take it in, so the word for beginning takes in the scrambled letters

parts.note: a beginning is a start

indicators.note: law-breaking reads as the word law being broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A loyal supporter is starting to tolerate crime.
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphen in 'law-breaking' hides the anagram signal 'breaking' inside what looks like one word; the scrambled law becomes LWA, and 'to accept' sets it within the beginning word.
explanation.definitionFit: A stalwart is a staunch, dependable supporter, which is what a loyalist is.

clue.text: Most of gossip is about kid of a particular group

indicators.note: is about means the shortened gossip word sits around the next piece
most of a word means all but its final letter is kept here

parts.note: a tale is a piece of gossip or tittle-tattle
to kid is to tease, which is to rib

explanation.surface: Much of the chatter concerns teasing within a certain clique.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Most of' leaves TAL, and 'is about' wraps that round the teasing word. 'kid' is the verb to tease, not a child.
explanation.definitionFit: Tribal describes what belongs to a tribe, a particular group of people sharing ties.

clue.text: Left a dog to drink eagerly

parts.note: a pup is a young dog

explanation.surface: Someone left a dog to drink its water greedily.
explanation.definitionFit: To lap up is to drink with the tongue keenly, and so to drink eagerly.

clue.text: George perhaps, and Paul too — it is fantastic!

indicators.note: fantastic suggests something fanciful and unreal, so the letters are reworked into a new form

explanation.surface: A Beatles fan raves about George and Paul.
explanation.walkthrough: The Beatles names point at Harrison and McCartney, but George is old RAF slang for an aircraft's automatic pilot. 'is fantastic' rearranges PAULTOO and IT.
explanation.definitionFit: George was the nickname airmen gave the automatic steering device that flies a plane, hence 'perhaps' for an example.

clue.text: Graduates invested in Mexican snack sauce

indicators.note: invested in means put inside, so the graduates go into the snack

parts.note: a taco is a folded tortilla, a Mexican snack
BAs are holders of the Bachelor of Arts degree, so graduates

explanation.surface: Graduates have put money into a Mexican snack and condiment business.
explanation.definitionFit: Tabasco is a brand of hot pepper sauce, a fiery condiment.

clue.text: Sanctimonious and risqué form of stealing

parts.note: pi is informal shorthand for pious, meaning sanctimonious
racy means risqué or slightly indecent

explanation.surface: A description of theft that is both preachy and naughty.
explanation.walkthrough: PI, short for pious, is a crossword favourite for sanctimonious.
explanation.definitionFit: Piracy is robbery at sea or the illegal copying of works, both kinds of theft.

clue.text: Showing embarrassment after father shaved

indicators.note: after means the blushing piece follows the parent in the answer

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father
someone embarrassed goes red in the face

explanation.surface: Someone blushed after Dad gave them a shave.
explanation.definitionFit: Pared means trimmed or cut thin, as when shaved down.

clue.text: Commercially-produced mature cheese is up

parts.note: fruit that is mature is ready to eat

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the cheese is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: Edam is a Dutch cheese

explanation.surface: A factory-made matured cheese has risen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is up' turns EDAM into MADE in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Ready-made goods are manufactured in advance for sale rather than made to order.

clue.text: Porter's rule for salad

parts.note: Cole Porter was the American songwriter, so his name gives Cole's
a law is a rule

explanation.surface: A songwriter's principle about what to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads like a scientific law named after a person, as in Murphy's Law.
explanation.definitionFit: Coleslaw is a salad of shredded raw cabbage in dressing.

clue.text: Sticker's almost green, dear

indicators.note: almost means the colour word stops one letter short

parts.note: lime is a shade of green
pet is a term of endearment like dear

explanation.surface: A label that is nearly green, darling.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is', a link. A limpet clings so tightly to rocks that it is a sticker.
explanation.definitionFit: A limpet is a shellfish famed for clinging to rocks, so a creature that sticks fast.

clue.text: Clinger-on lost balance crossing river

indicators.note: crossing means the scrambled letters span either side of the river letter
something lost is astray, so the letters wander into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone clinging on lost their footing while crossing a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lost' turns BALANCE into BANACLE, and 'crossing' puts R inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A barnacle is a crustacean that fixes itself to rocks and hulls, so something that clings on.

clue.text: Instruments for pot smokers?

parts.note: a pan is a cooking pot
pipes are things people smoke

explanation.surface: A joke about musical gear for cannabis users.
explanation.walkthrough: Pot suggests cannabis, so 'pot smokers' looks like drug users; it is a pan and pipes.
explanation.definitionFit: Panpipes are a wind instrument of graded reed tubes bound together.

clue.text: Positive response by doctor — though most sardonic

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held 'Positive response by doctor — though most sardonic' lacks the word ('initially', per the blog) that takes T from 'though'; without it no clue word signals the first-letter pick.
annotationWithheld.clue: Positive response by doctor — though most sardonic

clue.text: Fork out a wad (dollars), eating fine dish

indicators.note: eating means the scrambled letters take in the next piece
to fork out is to hand over and so to disperse, signalling the letters are scattered and rearranged

parts.note: F is the pencil-grading abbreviation for fine

explanation.surface: Paying a fortune for a meal of fine food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fork out' looks like paying up but signals the anagram, giving WALDORSALAD; 'eating' then takes in the fine letter. The surface's pricey meal echoes the luxury hotel where the dish was created.
explanation.definitionFit: Waldorf salad is a dish of apples, celery and walnuts in mayonnaise.

clue.text: Dull ladies mainly may accept a rise being out

indicators.note: accept means take in, so the shortened ladies word holds the next piece
mainly means most of the word is kept, here all but its last letter

parts.note: ladies are women

indicators.note: out means out of order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Tedious women might tolerate a pay rise not happening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mainly' leaves WOME, 'being out' gives EARIS, and 'may accept' sets that after the first letter. 'being out' suggests a pay rise not happening.
explanation.definitionFit: Wearisome means tiresome and tedious, the same as dull.

clue.text: Turned oars flat — hated reef being turbulent

indicators.note: turbulent means churned up, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Rowers in rough water near a hated reef.
explanation.walkthrough: In rowing, to feather is to turn the blade flat as it leaves the water.
explanation.definitionFit: Feathered in rowing means having turned the oar blades horizontal between strokes.

clue.text: Reference point for the Stars and Stripes, say

definitions.meaning: a benchmark against which things are measured
the American flag is an example of a banner or flag

explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link between the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: A standard is both a yardstick for comparison and a flag carried as an emblem.

clue.text: Takes out two sailors with energy for beef dish

indicators.note: out means out of place, so the letters of the first word are rearranged
two means the sailors word appears twice

parts.note: a tar is a sailor
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Someone takes a pair of seamen out for a hearty meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Steak tartare is a dish of raw minced beef, often topped with egg.

clue.text: Income for soldiers on location

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps
a venue is a location for an event

explanation.surface: Pay for troops stationed somewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: Revenue is income, especially that of a business or state.

clue.text: A French family with daughter showing no mercy

parts.note: un is French for a
kin are family
D is the abbreviation for daughter in genealogies

explanation.surface: A French household with a girl who is pitiless.
explanation.definitionFit: Unkind means harsh and lacking compassion, so showing no mercy.

clue.text: Ruined miners oddly missing items of clothing

indicators.note: oddly missing means the letters in odd positions are dropped, keeping the even ones

explanation.surface: Bankrupt miners lack some garments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ruined' looks like an anagram signal, but it is part of the letter run: the 2nd, 4th, 6th letters and so on are kept.
explanation.definitionFit: Undies is informal for underwear, items of clothing worn beneath others.

clue.text: Go to court — case of damage being material

parts.note: to sue is to take legal action in court

indicators.note: the case of a word is its outer shell, its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Suing over damage that matters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case of' keeps D and E, the outside of 'damage'.
explanation.definitionFit: Suede is leather with a napped finish, a fabric or material.

clue.text: Forceful macho types held in check

indicators.note: held in means the macho types sit inside the checking word

parts.note: to vet is to check thoroughly
he-men are macho, muscular types

explanation.surface: Tough guys are kept under control.
explanation.definitionFit: Vehement means intensely forceful or passionate.

clue.text: Drive from heath across top of town

indicators.note: across means the heath word stretches over the next letter, enclosing it

parts.note: a moor is open heathland

indicators.note: in a down clue the top of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A journey over the moor from the upper part of town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'top of' gives T from 'town', and 'across' puts it inside MOOR.
explanation.definitionFit: To motor is to drive a car, especially for pleasure.

clue.text: Name a European working for a military commander

parts.note: a Pole is a European from Poland
on means working, as a machine that is switched on

explanation.surface: Name a European employed by a general.
explanation.definitionFit: Napoleon Bonaparte was the French emperor and general, a famous military commander.

clue.text: Sell fifty per cent share of rare dog

indicators.note: fifty per cent share of means half of the word is kept, here its second half

parts.note: to dog someone is to follow them, which is to tail them

explanation.surface: Selling half a stake in an uncommon hound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dog' is a verb here, to follow, as private detectives tail a suspect.
explanation.definitionFit: To retail is to sell goods to the public in small quantities.

clue.text: Header misdirected — getting stick!

indicators.note: misdirected means sent the wrong way, so the letters go into a new order

explanation.surface: A footballer's poorly aimed header earns criticism.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stick' looks like 'getting stick', informal for criticism; it is the verb meaning cling, and 'getting' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To adhere is to stick fast to a surface.

clue.text: Adore old ruined city full of riches

indicators.note: ruined means wrecked, so the letters are broken up and rebuilt

explanation.surface: Someone loves an ancient ruined city crammed with treasure.
explanation.definitionFit: El Dorado was the legendary South American city of gold sought by conquistadors.
